summary: Convincing Industrial Age direction, four distinguishable occupations, and a strong Alderman. Approval is blocked by cap/hair intersections, trouser-like skirt construction, and shoulder capes buried in the bodies. The caravan leader needs a larger, unmistakable foreign railway identity.
problems: Workshop Mechanic: the low cap is embedded in the retained blocky hair; brown rectangular corners surround the grey crown instead of producing a clean cloth-cap silhouette.
Municipal Clerk: the lower skirt reads as two oversized trouser legs. The rectangular upper tier and divided lower slabs weaken the intended walking-skirt silhouette.
Market Provisioner: the lower apron is a single rigid hip-mounted board spanning both thighs. Its static fit does not establish clearance during walking.
Telegraph Messenger: the solid cone intersects the torso, leaving lateral shelves rather than a readable sloping pelerine. The distinctive upper-body garment largely disappears.
Railway Baron: the larger cone and red cylindrical edging similarly produce projecting tabs and a rigid hoop rather than a fitted travelling mantle.

Railway Baron: cream clothing establishes contrast, but the tiny luggage emblem does not clearly identify a distant railway magnate at stream scale. The low hat currently reads closer to a driver's cap.
fix:
Workshop Mechanic: Hide the default hair beneath the replacement cap, restoring only fitted side hair if needed. Widen and raise the flattened crown until it covers the scalp cleanly, with an unmistakable short forward peak. Retain the dark waistcoat, rolled sleeves and contrasting spanner bag.
Municipal Clerk: Replace the straight lower-leg boxes with shaped skirt gores: narrower above, gently flared toward a consistent hem, with a near-continuous silhouette at rest. Keep lower panels independently articulated and test their separation during walking; do not substitute a rigid shell across both legs. Preserve the puff sleeves, bun, small hat and cream ledger.
Market Provisioner: Retain the broad hat, cream bib and produce basket. Shorten the rigid hip-mounted apron section above the thigh-swing zone, then use two independently moving lower panels with a subtle central split. Check clearance against both thighs throughout the walk cycle.
Telegraph Messenger: Replace the solid cone with shallow sloping front and back cloth panels seated around the collar and shoulders. Attach any sleeve-covering side sections to the corresponding arms. Keep the hem above the armpits, with no horizontal ledges. Preserve the peaked cap, dispatch strap and pale gaiters.
Alderman: Keep the tall black top hat, dark frock coat, broad brass civic collar and oversized medallion. These already provide the clearest age and office signals; preserve their contrast and check chain-to-lapel clearance in animation.
Railway Baron: Remove the solid cone and cylindrical red hoop. Build a fitted travelling mantle from thin sloping panels, with vermilion edging following its actual hem. Give the hat a clear continuous bowler brim rather than a visor-like front. Repeat one bold foreign railway livery across hatband, mantle and luggage; place a large, legible winged wheel on the upper back where the elevated camera can see it. Retain the cream coat, cane and travel case.
